findings.category: permission_taxonomy_drift (not one of the 12 REVIEWER_PROTOCOL categories — a frontend/backend permission-key mismatch, architecture debt)
findings.evidence: Every `stock/*` sidebar/router entry falls back to the generic `items` permission key (permissionUrlForSidebarPath's `menuUrl.startsWith('stock/')` branch, line ~208), including `stock/raw-material-adjust`. The backend, however, gates the page's own read endpoint on the MORE SPECIFIC `items_show` (RawMaterialAdjustController.php:44) and writes on `items_create` (line 45) — neither of which is `items`. Confirmed empirically in this spec's own beforeAll comment (lines 92-108): a role granted `items_show` alone (backend-legit for history()) was silently redirected away from the page by the frontend router because the login payload's generic `items` permission had `access:false`; the test had to additionally grant the generic `items` key just to make the page reachable at all. This is the SAME class of bug the project already fixed once in the other direction on 2026-08-08 (`cash-overview`/`delivery-boy-cash-sessions` P1 'dead links': page shown, backend refuses) — here it manifests as the opposite direction (page hidden, backend would have served it). Since ALL `stock/*` routes share this generic fallback, this is not unique to RawMaterialAdjustComponent; any other `stock/*` page gated on a narrower permission than generic `items` at the backend would exhibit the same false-negative hide.
findings.fix_hint: Not a security defect (backend remains authoritative per-endpoint; worst case is a false-negative hide or, for the opposite mismatch direction, a navigable-but-erroring page shell — never unauthorized data disclosure, confirmed by reading resolvePermissionEntry/hasPermissionAccess's permissive-fallback-on-unknown-key design in resources/js/shared/permission-match.js). Recommend a follow-up sweep (same pattern as the 2026-08-08 fix) auditing every `MENU_URL_TO_PERMISSION_URL`-unmapped `stock/*` and `items/*` entry against its actual controller-level `permission:` middleware, adding explicit map entries where they diverge from the generic fallback. Does not block this wave's GREEN verdict — GStack's fixture correctly worked around it and it does not affect RawMaterialAdjustComponent's own security guarantee.

findings.category: silent_error (category 6, but scoped OUTSIDE the audited component)
findings.evidence: During state 07 (items_show-only readonly role viewing /admin/stock/raw-material-adjust), the captured network.json shows one unexpected `GET /api/admin/setting/item-category?paginate=0&order_column=id&order_type=asc` → 403, with a matching console.json `level:error` entry, and no visible `[role=alert]`/`.toast` in the DOM at that point (readonly panel + history render normally, the failure is fully silent to the user). Confirmed by reading RawMaterialAdjustComponent.vue directly that it contains ZERO references to `item-category` — the call originates from some other globally-mounted admin-layout widget (unidentified in this review's scope), not from the page under audit. ItemCategoryController::index gates on `permission:settings` (ItemCategoryController.php:27), which the readonly test role correctly lacks — so the 403 itself is semantically correct, only its silent (non-toasted) surfacing is the defect.
findings.fix_hint: Out of scope for D2 — pre-existing admin-layout-wide behavior triggered by any role lacking `settings`, not caused by the RawMaterialAdjustComponent change under audit. Flagging for a future dedicated wave (global admin-layout background-fetch audit) rather than blocking this wave; does not affect the correctness of anything asserted by this spec's 8 states.

findings.category: evidence_strength_nuance (meta-finding on the GStack report's own '4 independent proof layers' claim, not a product defect)
findings.evidence: Verified by reading app/Services/RawMaterials/RawMaterialStockService.php:118-158 (`mutate()`): the on_hand write and the movement insert happen atomically inside ONE `DB::transaction()`, and the 4 claimed proof layers break down as 3 genuinely distinct query surfaces, not 4: (1) the POST /adjust response body itself — proves nothing about persistence on its own; (2) the DOM stock card, fed by GET /stock/unified-overview → UnifiedStockViewService, which independently re-queries `raw_material_stock.on_hand` from a wholly separate controller/service — this IS a real independent persistence check; (3) the DOM history row and (4) the separate `adminApiContext.get(.../movements)` call both hit the EXACT SAME controller method (RawMaterialAdjustController::history()) and the same `raw_material_movements` query — they are two clients calling one endpoint, not two independent verifications of two different things. If history() had a bug that echoed request-derived values without correctly re-deriving them from a fresh persisted row, layers 3 and 4 would both be fooled identically. The claim's underlying conclusion (the write genuinely persisted) still holds because layer 2 independently confirms the `raw_material_stock` table value via a different table+service+controller, but 'four independently querying different things' overstates it by one — it is functionally three.
findings.fix_hint: Not a product bug. No action needed beyond noting the overstatement for future report calibration; the underlying functional proof (state 6 write actually persisting) is sound.

1_422_vs_403_claim.question: Is the 422-not-403 claim for state 5's negative-target bypass actually correct, and is 422 the semantically right code, or did GStack just accept whatever came back without understanding why?
1_422_vs_403_claim.verified: Read RawMaterialAdjustController.php:110-121 directly: `authorizeWritableBranchScope($request, $rawMaterial->branch_id)` runs FIRST (this is the 403-capable branch check) and passes for the admin API context used in state 5 (same branch). Only THEN does `$request->validate(['target_on_hand' => ['required','numeric','min:0','max:999999.999'], ...])` run — Laravel's `Request::validate()` throws `ValidationException`, which the framework's exception handler converts to HTTP 422 for JSON/API requests by default (standard Laravel behavior, not custom code in this controller). A negative number IS a validation failure (malformed input), not an authorization failure (right user, wrong data) — 422 is the semantically correct code per HTTP spec (422 Unprocessable Entity = well-formed request, semantically invalid; 403 = Forbidden regardless of content) and per this project's own REVIEWER_PROTOCOL allowlist which explicitly treats '422 on form validation submission' as expected, not an error. Confirmed the spec's own body assertion (`body.errors.target_on_hand` truthy, line 298) targets the FormRequest validation error shape specifically, not a generic abort message — this is not a code the test merely 'accepted', it asserts the specific validation-error payload shape that only a real `min:0` rule violation produces. The plan's original 'backend-403' assumption was simply wrong; GStack's correction is verified correct.

2_state6_math_and_proof_independence.question: Re-derive 50 → 37.25 = -12.75 independently, and verify the 4 claimed proof layers actually query different things (not 4 assertions on the same value that would all lie together).
2_state6_math_and_proof_independence.verified: 37.25 - 50 = -12.75, arithmetic confirmed correct and matches both the POST response's `delta` field assertion and the movement history row's '-12.75' text assertion (spec lines 331, 345, 359). Traced the write path in RawMaterialStockService::mutate() (lines 118-158): single DB::transaction() writes `raw_material_stock.on_hand` AND inserts `raw_material_movements` atomically — no window where one could succeed silently while the other fails without a full rollback. Found the '4 independent layers' framing overstates by one (see D2-003): layers 3 and 4 both hit RawMaterialAdjustController::history(), the same endpoint/query, just via two different Playwright clients (page DOM vs adminApiContext) — not two independently-implemented checks. Layer 2 (DOM stock card, fed by GET /stock/unified-overview → UnifiedStockViewService, a wholly separate controller reading `raw_material_stock.on_hand` fresh) IS a genuinely independent persistence check distinct from the movements-table checks. Net: 3 real independent query surfaces (write response / stock-table read / movements-table read), with the movements-table one exercised twice — the underlying functional proof is sound, the '4 independent' count is inflated by one. Logged as D2-003, P3, non-blocking.

3_branch_isolation_and_spoofability.question: Re-verify branch-2 genuinely cannot read or write branch-1 material via direct API, and check whether branch scoping is spoofable via a request parameter rather than server-side session/token binding.
3_branch_isolation_and_spoofability.verified: Read AdminController.php:15-41 (`authorizeBranchScope` / `authorizeWritableBranchScope`) directly: both compare `(int) $user->branch_id` — resolved server-side from `$request->user()` (Sanctum token → authenticated model, NOT any client-supplied field) — against `$branchId`, which in RawMaterialAdjustController is `(int) $rawMaterial->branch_id`, itself resolved via Laravel route-model binding from the DB row the `{rawMaterial}` route segment points to, again NOT a client-supplied body/query parameter. There is no code path where a request body field like `branch_id` influences either comparison — confirmed by grep, `branch_id` never appears in the controller's `$request->validate()` rule set (only `target_on_hand`, `reason`, `note`). Re-ran state 08 twice (see point 5): branch-2 token → adjust 403, movements(history) 403, and the post-attempt DB check confirms zero write landed (`finalBody.movements[0].reason !== 'cross-branch attempt'`). Branch scoping here is genuinely non-spoofable — it is bound to the authenticated Sanctum principal, not a request parameter.

4_permission_gate_generic_items_mismatch.question: Is the items/items_show frontend-vs-backend permission-key mismatch actually fine (defense in depth), or does it reveal a pattern that could let a wrongly-scoped role see a page it shouldn't on some OTHER less-tested page?
4_permission_gate_generic_items_mismatch.verified: Read permissionUrlForSidebarPath (BackendMenuComponent.vue) directly: EVERY `stock/*` route defaults to the generic `items` permission key unless explicitly overridden in MENU_URL_TO_PERMISSION_URL — this is not unique to raw-material-adjust, it is the blanket default for the whole stock section. Traced both possible mismatch directions: (a) narrower backend permission than generic `items` (this page's case, items_show/items_create) → frontend HIDES a page the backend would have served — a false negative, functionally broken but not a security leak; (b) broader backend permission than generic `items` was already fixed once for cash-overview/delivery-boy-cash-sessions on 2026-08-08 after it caused visible-but-403'ing 'dead links' for real cashier accounts — also not a data leak, since Laravel's `permission:X` middleware checks the EXACT permission name (no fuzzy/prefix matching), so a role missing the specific backend permission gets a hard 403 on the underlying API call regardless of what the frontend router decided to show. In neither direction did I find a path where the SPA renders sensitive DATA (not just a navigable shell) without a matching backend-authorized API call succeeding — this is a Vue SPA that fetches everything over HTTP, no server-rendered secrets embedded in the initial payload for this page. JUDGMENT: this does NOT rise to a security finding — the backend is confirmed authoritative per-endpoint in both mismatch directions, consistent with CLAUDE.md §9's own note that FormRequest/controller-level authz is the unified source of truth. It IS a real, systemic UX/architecture-debt pattern (same root cause fixed once before, now recurring in the opposite direction) that deserves a dedicated backlog sweep across all `stock/*`/`items/*` routes rather than one-off patches whenever a tester happens to trip over it — logged as D2-001, P2, non-blocking for this wave.

5_fresh_reruns.question: Re-run the spec twice and the PHPUnit endpoint test fresh, independent of GStack's own report.
5_fresh_reruns.verified: `php artisan test --filter=RawMaterialAdjustEndpointTest` → 11/11 passed (3.00s), fresh run by this reviewer. `npx playwright test tests/e2e/verif-globale-raw-material-adjust-2026-08-14.spec.js --project=chromium` run TWICE back-to-back against the local dev server (127.0.0.1:8000) → 8/8 passed both times (21.7s, then 22.7s), confirming the idempotent seed/cleanup claim (force-delete + firstOrCreate discipline holds across repeat runs, no unique-index collisions on the 2nd pass).
